licoes.objectivo: Dizer a mesma coisa em três registos.

exercicios.enunciado: Ligue cada palavra formal à neutra ou coloquial.
Which sentence is formal?

opcoes.texto: I regret to inform you that the opening has been postponed.
Bad news, the opening's slipped a bit.
The opening is two weeks late.

exercicios.enunciado: Which sentence is colloquial?

opcoes.texto: We've pushed the opening back a couple of weeks.
The opening has been postponed until 29 October.
Please be advised of a change of date.

exercicios.enunciado: Which sentence is neutral?

opcoes.texto: The opening is now on 29 October, two weeks later than planned.
We regret to inform you of a postponement.

exercicios.enunciado: You send "We regret to inform you…" to a close colleague. She will probably think…
Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: Should you [require] further details, I would be happy to arrange a call.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: We've pushed the opening [back] a couple of weeks.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: Coffee later? I'll fill you [in].

exercicios.enunciado: A abertura foi adiada até 29 de Outubro.
exercicios.resposta: The opening has been postponed until 29 October.

exercicios.frase: This is Thandi. Register isn't decoration. Get it wrong one way, you sound rude. Get it wrong the other way, you sound cold.
exercicios.enunciado: What does Thandi say about register?

opcoes.texto: The wrong register can sound rude or cold.

exercicios.frase: The opening has been postponed until the twenty-ninth of October. We've pushed it back a couple of weeks.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita: primeiro formal, depois coloquial.
Your office will be closed next Monday because of a water problem. Tell the news to an important client (formal), to your team (neutral) and to a close colleague (colloquial).
exercicios.frase: Should you
exercicios.resposta: To the client: our office will be closed on Monday due to repairs. Should you require assistance, please call our emergency number. To the team: the office is closed on Monday, please work from home. To my colleague: no water on Monday, so no office!

exercicios.enunciado: Is English more formal or less formal at work than your first language? Give an example.
exercicios.frase: example
exercicios.resposta: Less formal, I think. In Portuguese, I write "Exmo. Senhor" to a director. In English, "Dear Mr Sithole" is enough, and colleagues use first names. For example, my English-speaking boss signs e-mails with just his first name.

licoes.titulo: The ball is in their court
licoes.objectivo: Usar expressões idiomáticas do trabalho com o sentido e o registo certos.

exercicios.enunciado: Ligue cada expressão ao sentido.

pares.a: the ball is in their court

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: We've done everything. The ball's in their [court].

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: Let's call it a [day].

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: If we lose, it's back to square [one].

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: Then bite the [bullet] and ask him tomorrow.

exercicios.enunciado: "There's an elephant in the room." This means…

opcoes.texto: There is a problem nobody wants to talk about.

exercicios.enunciado: "Are we on the same page?" This means…

opcoes.texto: Do we agree and have the same information?
Are we reading the same book?
Are we in the same office?

exercicios.enunciado: When is it better NOT to use idioms?

opcoes.texto: with listeners who may not know them, and in formal letters

exercicios.enunciado: "It's a win-win." This is…

exercicios.frase: I'm Rajesh. The price was fair, the references are strong, and we reported the consultant. If they're honest, it's a win-win.
exercicios.enunciado: Why does Rajesh think it is a win-win?

opcoes.texto: Mussiro gets a good team and Mopane gets the contract.

exercicios.frase: This is Nuno. Last week I told Inês a delay was not my cup of tea. She translated it word for word.
exercicios.enunciado: What happened when Nuno used an idiom with Inês?

opcoes.texto: She translated it word for word and misunderstood.

exercicios.frase: The ball's in their court. Let's call it a day.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita, com o acento em "court" e "day".
Tell a colleague about a decision you are waiting for, using at least four idioms naturally. Then say the most important sentence again in plain English.
exercicios.frase: square one
exercicios.resposta: I've applied for a transfer to Benguela. The ball's in their court now. If they say no, it's back to square one. It could be a win-win. The elephant in the room is my manager, so I'll bite the bullet and tell her. In plain English: I'm waiting for their decision.

exercicios.enunciado: Should people in international teams avoid idioms? Why, or why not?
exercicios.frase: plain English
exercicios.resposta: Mostly yes. Idioms are for people who share them. In an international team, plain English is clearer and more respectful. With native speakers, a few idioms are fine.

licoes.objectivo: Usar linguagem vaga e aproximativa de forma natural, no registo certo.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: We ran the test about fifty times, give or [take].

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: It crashed at seven[ish].

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: A hundred or [so] people are coming.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: There were a [bunch] of journalists.

exercicios.enunciado: "It sort of works." This means it…
Where is "four million-ish" NOT appropriate?

opcoes.texto: in a report to the board

exercicios.enunciado: Choose the correct sentence.

opcoes.texto: Thirty or so of people came.

exercicios.enunciado: The formal version of "fifty or so" is…
Ele tem trinta e tal anos e vive em Luanda.
exercicios.resposta: He's thirty-ish and he lives in Luanda.

exercicios.frase: I'm Lindiwe. It sort of works. It crashed twice, at sevenish and again after lunch.
exercicios.enunciado: How many times did the software crash?

exercicios.frase: This is Bongani. As it happens, Durban offered me a job last week. I turned it down.
exercicios.enunciado: What did Bongani do with the job offer from Durban?

exercicios.frase: A hundred or so. At sevenish. It sort of works.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita, de forma descontraída.
A friend asks about your last weekend or a recent trip. Tell them, relaxed and natural, with at least five vague expressions (or so, -ish, give or take, sort of, a bunch of, loads of, and so on).
exercicios.frase: or so
exercicios.resposta: It was great! We drove to Cabo Ledo on Saturday, left at sixish, three hours give or take. There were loads of people, a bunch of surfers and so on. The fish was kind of expensive but amazing. We got home around nine or so.

exercicios.enunciado: Does vague language sound lazy, or does it sound natural? When?
exercicios.frase: natural
exercicios.resposta: It sounds natural with friends, because nobody needs exact numbers over drinks. It sounds lazy in a report or with a client, where people need to trust your numbers.

licoes.objectivo: Usar phrasal verbs separáveis e de três partes com o objecto na posição certa.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.

exercicios.frase: The Luanda office opens in January. Lerato will set [it up].

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.

exercicios.enunciado: Choose the correct sentence.
Choose the correct sentence.

opcoes.texto: I can't put up with it.
I can't put it up with.
I can't put up it with.

exercicios.enunciado: Choose the correct sentence.

opcoes.texto: Rajesh will look after the money.
Rajesh will look the money after.

exercicios.enunciado: The formal equivalent of "turn down an offer" is…
Ela teve a ideia de metade do plano.
exercicios.resposta: She came up with half of the plan.

exercicios.frase: I'm Nuno. Inês takes over Mozambique. I'm handing the Mussiro relationship over to her completely.
exercicios.enunciado: What is Nuno handing over to Inês?

exercicios.frase: This is Nuno. I don't want to put it off. Rumours are already going round.
exercicios.enunciado: Why does Nuno want to tell the team soon?

opcoes.texto: Dr Mthembu asked him to wait.

exercicios.frase: Turn it down. Set it up. Hand it over.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita, com o acento na partícula.
Describe a change at work, at school or at home with at least five phrasal verbs, including two with a pronoun in the middle and one three-part verb.
exercicios.frase: put up with
exercicios.resposta: Our school set up a computer room. The old director turned the idea down twice. When the new director took over, she came up with a plan: parents donated laptops. We fixed them up and handed them over. The internet is slow, but we put up with it.

exercicios.enunciado: Should a manager ask the team before a reorganisation, or decide and then explain? Why?
exercicios.frase: because
exercicios.resposta: Ask first, at least the people most affected, because they often come up with better ideas. Then the manager decides and explains. Nuno talked to Lerato and Bongani before he set it up.

"I gotta go." In full, this is…

exercicios.resposta: He's a bit under the weather today.

exercicios.enunciado: Tell a friend about a surprising event in your life, something that happened out of the blue, using at least four idioms from this lesson.
exercicios.frase: out of the blue
exercicios.resposta: Last month, out of the blue, an old school friend called me. I was a bit under the weather, but we met for lunch. Breaking the ice was a piece of cake. She asked me to join her business. I'm still on the fence. It's a long shot.

exercicios.enunciado: Should English courses teach idioms, or focus on plain international English? Why?
exercicios.frase: plain
exercicios.resposta: Both. Learners must understand common idioms, because they hear them every day. But for speaking, plain international English is safer.

exercicios.frase: You look like someone who doesn't know anyone. Me neither.

At a networking event, someone says: "You look like you need rescuing from that corner." Answer, introduce yourself, make small talk, find something in common, and end politely.
exercicios.frase: gotta
exercicios.resposta: Ha! Is it that obvious? I'm Ana, I work in logistics at a cement company. Oh, you're in transport too? Small world. Listen, it's been great to meet you. I've gotta go and say hello to my boss, but here's my card. Let's grab a coffee sometime.

exercicios.enunciado: Do you enjoy networking events, or do you find them difficult? Why?
exercicios.frase: because
exercicios.resposta: I find them difficult at first, because I don't like talking to strangers. But once I find one thing in common, it gets easier. Kind of like breaking the ice at a party.

Your department will move to a new building in two months. Tell it to your director (formal), to your team (neutral), and to a close friend (colloquial, with a vague expression and an idiom).
exercicios.frase: win-win
exercicios.resposta: To the director: the relocation has been scheduled for 1 December, over a weekend, with no additional budget. To the team: we're moving on the first of December, over a weekend. To my friend: we're finally moving, December-ish. Air conditioning that works, total win-win.

exercicios.enunciado: Tell your team in English what this note says: "A partir de 1 de Novembro, o horário de atendimento passa a ser das 8h às 16h, de segunda a sexta. Aos sábados, só por marcação. Os colaboradores afectados serão contactados pelos recursos humanos."
exercicios.frase: appointment
exercicios.resposta: From the first of November, we're open from eight to four, Monday to Friday. On Saturdays, it's by appointment only. If this affects your hours, HR will contact you.

Tell the same piece of news (a new manager arrives next month) to your manager and then to a close friend.
exercicios.frase: Guess what
exercicios.resposta: To my manager: I understand the new manager will start on the first of next month; I'd be happy to help with the handover. To my friend: Guess what? We're getting a new boss next month. Fingers crossed she's nice!

exercicios.enunciado: Use a phrasal verb with a pronoun, an idiom and a vague expression to describe your week.
exercicios.frase: or so
exercicios.resposta: Busy! A client asked for a new report, so I had to put my holiday off. I finally handed it in on Thursday. Twenty pages or so. Now the ball's in their court.
